text:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + streaming disconnect rate detected for /v1/streams (us-west-2). 3.1% early terminations in last 5m, baseline 0.2%. paging on-call.

sam_h: got the page, joining. seeing the spike on the streaming success_rate graph. errors are mostly 'chunked encoding error' and 'client canceled connection'.

nina_k: logs show a lot of `upstream prematurely closed connection` from runtime-node-* and some EPIPE in the nginx proxy. starting tail now.

alex_p: tagging likely-cause: we've been rolling the new http-parser patch earlier today to improve throughput. version diff: 2026-03-14T10:12 UTC. rolling back candidate?

julia_r: PD: sam_h is on-call. sam, are we already escalating to infra? @oncall-rotation if sam needs help.

sam_h: I want to triage first. looking at trace_ids for failed streams. many fail after first chunk, 200ms-1s after initial headers. client side sees truncated stream.

eng-sre-bot: metric spike: streaming_disconnect_rate /v1/streams from 0.2% -> 3.1% (5m window). p95 response time unaffected. upstream_worker_restarts increased on runtime-node-2 and -3.

nina_k: copy of a failing log snippet:
```
2026-03-14T15:20:11.423Z runtime-node-2 stream_id=abcd1234 ERROR: write failed: EPIPE
2026-03-14T15:20:11.423Z nginx[pid] upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
2026-03-14T15:20:11.424Z proxy timeout? keepalive reset
```

alex_p: also seeing intermittent ECONNRESET between nginx and runtime. Not seeing application exceptions. memory looks ok.

sam_h: quick mitigations we can try: 1) increase upstream keepalive timeout and proxy_buffering off for /v1/streams 2) temporarily route streaming traffic to the canary that still runs old parser 3) scale up streaming worker pool to absorb flapping.

julia_r: customer impact: two large customers reported truncated chunks in their analytics pipelines, one has partial responses causing business logic retries. CS ops notified. @cs-ops please collect affected request ids from customers.

cs-ops: collecting, will paste list shortly. their SDKs show early connection close errors.

nina_k: I'm going to flip proxy buffering off for streams (nginx conf) on us-west-2 as a low-risk change. will patch in 60s and watch. command: `kubectl -n infra set configmap nginx-proxy --from-file=us-west-2-streams.conf` then rolling update.

sam_h: good. also enable debug logs on runtime-node-2/3 for stream handshakes and kv cache writes.

(2m later)

eng-sre-bot: config change applied in us-west-2: proxy_buffering: off for /v1/streams. rollout 3/3 pods.

sam_h: observing immediate drop: disconnect rate down to 1.0% in 2m. still above baseline but improving. upstream worker restarts decreased.

alex_p: rolling routing: sending 30% of streaming traffic to old-parser canary. no spike there. suggests parser change correlated.

nina_k: capturing tcpdump between nginx and runtime for one failing pod. saving to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1723456789.pcap.

julia_r: CS update: customer A confirmed partial responses reduced after change, their ingestion has fewer retries. they want postmortem.

sam_h: next steps: 1) keep proxy_buffering off for 1 hour as mitigation 2) stop the in-prod parser rollout and revert to previous http-parser on runtime nodes 3) run regression tests for chunked transfer unit and connection pipelining 4) complete incident ticket and customer comms.

oncall-rotation: Handoff at 16:00 UTC to nina_k. Sam -> Nina: all mitigation actions documented in the incident. if things re-escalate, page infra lead @alex_p.

(1h later)

eng-sre-bot: after revert completed: streaming_disconnect_rate back to 0.18% (within baseline). all runtime nodes stable.

sam_h: incident mitigated. creating postmortem ticket: INC-2026-1723456789. brief: parser rollout caused intermittent upstream closes when chunked responses were produced under certain header ordering. mitigation: rollback, proxy buffering off, increase keepalive. long-term: add end-to-end streaming tests, canary gating for parser changes, and a synthetic stream monitor that checks chunk integrity.

julia_r: sending customer-facing summary to CS for review. cc: oncall and eng-sre.

cs-ops: confirmed customers notified. they appreciated the quick rollback.

sam_h: closing thread, will add detailed timelines in the postmortem doc and link to pcaps and debug logs. :white_check_mark:
